articles.title: Tech layoffs 2026: Tracking the job losses across Disney, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, Meta and others
articles.summary: There are only a few weeks left in the year and there have been more than 200,000 job losses across the tech industry. Here are the details.
articles.body:
2026 is almost over, but unfortunately we didn't get here without a ton of tech layoffs. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. Microsoft 's round of layoffs in July affected 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Shortly after, companies including Samsung, Amazon, Uber and Monday.com followed suit.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." In addition, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 200,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Disney is reportedly planning to lay off thousands in an effort to cut annual costs by 20%. Layoffs have not been confirmed yet, but we'll update this story if and when they are. According to people familiar with the matter, the cost reductions could come from layoffs in addition to expense reductions.

Polymarket staff reportedly experienced layoffs, but the scope of which is not known. The reports also suggest the company has reduced the number of contractors it will work with moving forward, particularly in the marketing department.

Squarespace, the website-building company, is laying off 19% of its workforce, which amounts to about 300 people. "The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth," Jeff Seedman, a representative from Squarespace, told TechCrunch. Squarespace's industry has been disrupted by AI, as "vibe-coding" website builders have become more popular.

Design software company Canva's recent layoffs will impact 22% of its staff, or just over 1,200 employees. According to reports , the company is reorganizing its business and merging its product, growth and platform teams. Canva is also looking to reduce "subspecialisation," which could result in remaining employees taking on more responsibilities.

Fintech company Block started its second round of layoffs recently, after cutting more than 4,000 jobs earlier this year. According to reports , the Jack Dorsey-led company hasn't disclosed how many jobs were affected this time around, but reportedly teams at Cash App and Square (both owned by Block) were affected.

Amazon reportedly laid off "fewer than 1,000 white-collar workers" in its stores division. That's the part of the company that oversees the tech giant's e-commerce website. Employees in the U.S., India and the United Kingdom were reportedly affected.

In an additional incident, Amazon laid off about 250 employees in its devices and services unit, according to a Reuters report . This comes after a number of new product announcements, including new Kindles and Echo devices . According to the report, the cuts mostly affect those in software development.

The cloud storage company Dropbox is laying off about 9% of its workforce, which accounts for roughly 200 employees. The job cuts primarily affect workers on the engineering, product, design, and G&A teams. "Today, we're making difficult choices about where we invest and how we organize Dropbox to achieve the product and growth priorities that will matter most for our long-term strategy," Dropbox co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi said in an email to staff. Alkarmi also announced that, alongside the layoffs, chief technology officer Ali Dasdan will step down.

While not officially new layoffs just yet, reports claim Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees. This is in an effort to further reduce costs in the wake of increased AI usage. According to the reports, Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance divisions will be participating in the offer. Microsoft already laid off thousands of workers so far in 2026.

EBay will reportedly cut 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations. The latest job cuts come after a previous round of layoffs back in February, which affected about 800 positions. "As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," an eBay spokesperson said in a statement.

Vide game publisher EA will eliminate 400 jobs , or about 3% of its workforce. This includes shutting down BioWare , the development studio behind the Mass Effect games. The next Mass Effect title will be cancelled as a result of the layoffs. These job cuts come after EA told investors earlier this year that it would reduce research and development costs as part of a plan to save upwards of $700 million.

According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, Netflix will lay off about 1,000 people, which accounts for about 6% of its global workforce. The report says the bulk of the layoffs will affect Netflix's "product, tech, legal and human-resources teams." This latest round of layoffs is the biggest for the company since 2022, and it comes in the wake of Netflix struggling to increase customer engagement and overall growth.

A "large part" of the Airtable team was laid off on October 12. Federico Simionato, Airtable owner Bending Spoons' product leader, said on X that the layoffs were not due to the workers' abilities but rather the company's "deep belief that small teams ship more and better." The exact number of employees affected by the layoffs wasn't disclosed.

Workday will be laying off around 140 employees from the Bay Area, as part of an effort to trim its tech team. The cuts come as part of a broader plan to cut the company's global workforce by 2.5%.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Season 3 Loses a Bit of Steam This Week With a Pair of Very Talky Episodes
articles.summary: The Rings of Power loses some forward momentum this week with two very talky episodes where several characters are literally waiting around for something to happen.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 5-6.

The Rings of Power Season 3 loses some forward momentum this week with two very talky episodes where several characters are literally waiting around for something to happen, whether it’s Sauron trying to pry secrets out of Celeborn or the rival Númenórean factions camped across from each other and poised for battle. The closing moments of Episode 306 definitely pick up the pace, though, promising an eventful finish to this season in next week’s final two episodes.

Gil-galad and Elrond’s mission to Númenór to coax Pharazôn into their war against Sauron sees them weighing their options, including the possibility of asking Miriel to rescind her claim to the throne. Ultimately, though, it’s Pharazôn himself who offers to cease hostilities with Miriel by proposing marriage to her. Ick.

That certainly sucks for Miriel – we saw how things went earlier this season for Pharazôn’s previous wife, Eärien – but, for the story, it seems like the only way to resolve this plodding subplot and finally get all the players on the battlefield against Sauron.

Elrond and Gil-galad haven’t been particularly compelling characters this season, but it was nice to see Elrond revisit his past and what his brother Elros meant to him and to the Númenóreans. Indeed, complicated feelings between loved ones and things that had long been left unsaid is a throughline in these episodes not only with Elrond and Elros but also with Galadriel and Celeborn and Durin and Disa as the latter two married couples wrestle with mistakes from the past.

Poor Marnûkh, meanwhile, learns there is a fate worse than death as Sauron slays his children and then leaves him to be tortured. Torture is also used on Celeborn after he’s captured, with the Elf lord getting the Giles Corey treatment . Ultimately, Celeborn is tricked into revealing to Sauron what the missing ingredients are needed to successfully forge the One Ring. That Galadriel-to-Sauron kiss with Celeborn will surely become a gif in no time.

Gandalf’s mission to help Pallando see the light sure didn’t work out well for him, did it? Pallando violently rebuffs Gandalf and sends him away strapped to the back of an oliphaunt. Although I know Gandalf hasn’t reached his full power and potential yet, it was still a bit disappointing to see the Dark Wizard make such quick work of him. I hope the storyline between them can be resolved this season but I suspect it will probably get dragged out into Season 4.

He’s only been a Ring-servant for like a weekend but Theo is already suffering from buyer’s remorse. Galadriel taking pity on him sure is big of her considering he killed Arondir , which makes me suspect Theo will be given a redemptive death in the season finale.

That wouldn’t shock me since this season seems intent on killing off original characters who were introduced in Season 1, whittling the cast down to just the core Tolkien-created characters as the war against Sauron picks up. By doing so, the show is signaling to audiences, “Don’t worry. We know many of you didn’t like these characters, so we’re just gonna make the show more like the movies now.”

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Parties, Murals, and Anxiety — What It's Like to Launch a GTA Game
articles.summary: What's it like to launch a GTA game? We spoke to former Rockstar developers to find out.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is finally coming on November 19 and is already breaking records. It’s the most anticipated video game launch of all time and on track to be the most successful entertainment product ever released. The pressure must be unimaginable for the people working at developer and publisher Rockstar as the entire world’s gaze looks them squarely in the eyes.

So, what’s it like to launch one of the biggest pieces of entertainment of all time? Is it scary? Is it fun? How anxious does it make you? Well, it largely depends on where you’re based.

For former Rockstar researcher Gregory Johnson, who lived in New York and travelled all over the world to document criminals and culture for Dan Houser and the rest of GTA 5’s writing team for 16 years, it meant attending a private mashup concert for Rockstar’s devs, friends and family at the Lincoln Center, headlined by German electronic music band Tangerine Dream and hip hop producers Alchemist and Oh No. “It was just grand in scale,” Johnson told me during a recent IGN interview.

For designer Matt Freedman, who worked out of Toronto, Canada, it was a different experience. “There was certainly a party culture around Rockstar, but the wrap parties were generally the tamer kind of thing,” he said. “They were nice. They were very fancy, but it kind of became a formula after a while — the young guys love it because you're going to a fancy restaurant and you get all the food you can eat and all you can drink.”

Mike York, who worked at Rockstar New England as an animator for five years, barely saw anything at all. There was a big party for the developers when GTA 5 launched, but his biggest memory of that time though came from being in a local bar with his friends.

“The trailer came up, and it showed some of my animation,” York said. “It was Trevor stomping on the toilet — something like that. I was like, ‘Oh my god! Look, look, look, look, look, look, look! That's the game I'm working on. That's my s**t right there. That's my animation, dude.’ We're like freaking out at the bar, you know. That was the only time I saw GTA 5 where I was living. We were in a small town in New England. It's called Andover, Massachusetts. It's a small place, and there's no big murals going up there.”

Of course, there’s going to be some disparity. New York is the beating heart of Rockstar Games, its head office, despite the company originating from Scotland. When he wasn’t on a ride along with police through Mexican gang territory for GTA research , Gregory Johnson was in a passenger seat on the bridge of the Rockstar mothership. He saw the evolution of Rockstar’s launch process from the command center itself, and watched that process evolve from the release of San Andreas through to Red Dead Redemption 2.

“Starting with GTA San Andreas, there was this playbook where they would do these huge murals around the city and around other cities,” Johnson said. “They're doing that right now with GTA 6. Well, they have mastered it at this point. This is like the final form of everything I saw. But when they started with GTA San Andreas, they would do a lot of huge murals. They would have these amazing midnight launch events, where they would bring in game journalists and various influencers for first looks at the gameplay.

“That playbook, as I understand it, started with GTA San Andreas. Although that was, frankly, the first Rockstar game I worked on. GTA 4 was set in New York City, so it was an opportunity for us to build out a GTA that was right in our backyard — unlike GTA 3, which had East Coast vibes, they got more and more true to the city that inspired the game.”

Instead of jumping on a plane to go on research trips, suddenly Johnson was hopping on a train out to Greenpoint, Brooklyn, Harlem, or Queens to spend time among the various enclaves of America’s most diverse melting pot. As launch closed in, he started to see “wanted” posters for GTA 4 protagonist Niko Bellic popping up around the different boroughs, his work life bleeding into his surroundings.

“There was a lot of stuff that basically borrowed from what hip hop street teams would do,” Johnson explained. “So that's what the wanted posters were and the Rockstar stickers all over the city, and doing the grand murals. We had people like DJ Premier run an exclusive event around the time of launch at APT, a club that was near and dear to my heart at that time. People came up to SiriusXM Satellite Radio where another hip hop DJ, Green Lantern, had his show, and I think Premiere came through for that as well. They had live gameplay, and people calling in — just building up the drama all over New York, and really getting the city behind it.”

Rockstar has gone even more all-out for GTA 6, with massive Vice City-themed blimps, modded cars to look like the in-game models driving around Miami, taking over the Kaseya Center and putting the local NBA team in a Vice City kit to celebrate GTA 6’s upcoming launch. But even before all of that, the city of Miami was ready for Rockstar’s return — despite the last GTA game set in Vice City launching more than 20 years ago.

“I remember when we were doing research trips [for GTA 6] around South Florida, in Miami in particular, even at that time in 2016 there were murals paying homage to Vice City, people calling their businesses Vice City,” Johnson explained. “For [Rockstar] it was still a little bit stunning, the degree to which Miami embraced this alternate identity of itself is Vice City. The fact that they embraced it as a part of the city's identity really gave Rockstar the green light.”

Before all the celebrations, the murals, the city coming out to celebrate the game, though, there was the fear. According to Matt Freedman, there was anxiety in the air at Rockstar as it prepared to launch GTA 5.

Unlike movies, where you can see through the viewfinder and get an idea of how your film looks, video games are in utero until right at the end of the project. “GTA 5 came together about two months before launch,” he said. Things get changed and cut, previously separate parts are stitched together, and only right at the end do these disparate parts meld and you find out whether you’ve made something worthwhile. Considering the long development times of these sprawling, ambitious open world games with complex NPC behaviors, simulated physics and epic stories, it’s no wonder there’s some trepidation.

“Launching a Rockstar game, it's very much running a marathon for like six years,” Freedman explained. “You're going at a very deliberate, very steady pace. You're just rocking those 60 to 80-hour work weeks, and you're in that groove. They're very large, very complex projects. Rockstar's got its process figured out quite well. But in all the Rockstar games I'd worked on, we're all in a bit of a panic up until launch. Probably the best example was Grand Theft Auto Online. No one thought that thing was gonna work, man. Everyone was like, ‘Thank God we got single-player because our online certainly is lame.’ We had two hours of content, a very small amount of content at the start.

“Rockstar to their credit just kept working on it. It got a little bit of heat, got a little bit of excitement, and then they kept building on it. You never really know exactly what's going to work and what's not going to work. You can be super conservative and give people what they wanted yesterday, and it's not what they want today, and I think to Rockstar's credit, they're very willing to try new ideas and try new things."

Around five months before GTA 5’s launch, another problem appeared. The developers realized they’d budgeted real-time lighting for cutscenes incorrectly, which would have caused major performance issues on PS3 and Xbox 360. Every single cutscene (double digit hours of scenes) had the problem, lit with one environment light and five point lights — the latter had to be reduced down to two. The cutscene team had to relight every single cutscene in the game before the launch deadline.

“To the cutscene team's credit, and to the lighting artist's credit, they got it done, and those cutscenes look fantastic,” Freedman said. “Man, I would have loved to have seen it with them with the original lighting setup. I don't know if they ever got a chance to put that back in there [with the next-gen version]. I don't think they did, but the old ones must have looked spectacular, considering how good the current ones look.”

On the animation side, things had slowed right down. According to former animator Mike York, animators and artists become “glorified QA” for the final stretch because the game goes on lockdown and no new elements are allowed to be added. Instead, they work through the game looking for bugs, helping the QA department polish things up for release. Until one day, when a message came down from the top of the company: we’re adding first-person.

“They were like, ‘We’re adding first-person mode,’” York explained. “We’re like, ‘What?’ You don’t do that — you don’t just come in and add first-person mode. There's thousands of animations that need to be created, and thousands of animations that need to be adjusted or redone in a different way and re-exported and and put in so that you could use that one instead of the other one, and it caused a ton of work for everyone.”

Eventually, GTA 5 would ship without first-person support because of the time it took to implement. It only came as a feature when the next-gen version dropped on PS4 and Xbox One.

“It's like pushing anything new out into the world,” Johnson added. “The closer you get to that moment, it's a natural human thing to feel a lot of anxiety and breathless anticipation. But I think there is, especially after all of these years, a certain degree of faith in the process. This company has wildly succeeded in the past.

“One of the things that Dan Houser always told us as a research team was that we've got to get buy-in inside the building as much as possible in order to get buy-in outside of the building. So we’ve got to be true believers in our own product. So a lot of the work we did was just you know raising the cultural IQ across the company as much as possible. Like with anything else, if you feel like you've done all this preparation and all this hard work, and you've got a great plan, and you've got a great track record, and a very capable marketing team, I think you've got to trust your work.”

After two delays, GTA 6 finally launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19. Marketing for the next title has already ramped up, with the city of Miami plastered in murals and advertisements for Rockstar’s long-anticipated open world crime sequel.

Millions have been spent on getting the word out there for a game that’s reportedly already earned $1 billion in preorders alone and become the most preordered game in the history of PlayStation and Xbox. For context, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is the highest grossing opening for a movie of all time, and it didn’t even make half that much in its opening weekend. GTA 6 is a behemoth unlike anything we’ve seen.

That’s reflected in the marketing, which knows it already has the gamers and is attempting to seduce the rest of the world with flashy, over-the-top activations. NBA team the Miami Heat will wear Vice City-themed jerseys for a match around the game’s launch. The top of the Kaseya Center , home of The Heat, was lit up to usher in the collaboration between Rockstar and Miami’s home team. Real life cars are being modded to look like their GTA 6 counterparts and driven around Miami before being auctioned off for $1.3 million. If there’s anxiety at the studio over GTA 6, Rockstar isn’t showing it.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: 'We're Getting GTA 6 First': New Zealand Trick Celebrated by Country's Official Tourist Board
articles.summary: New Zealand's official tourism board has celebrated the launch of GTA 6 by welcoming gamers taking advantage of the infamous New Zealand trick.
articles.body:
New Zealand's official tourism board has celebrated the launch of GTA 6 by welcoming gamers taking advantage of the infamous New Zealand trick.

Countless GTA 6 fans are expected to take advantage of the cheeky Xbox loophole where you can quickly switch your console to another region and gain access to new releases slightly earlier. GTA 6 doesn't officially launch until midnight wherever you are... well, it is midnight earlier in New Zealand than likely wherever you're ready this. (Unless you are in New Zealand, in which case, hello!)

Hilariously, the New Zealand trick has become so popular that the country itself is now acknowledging it, as well as the numerous GTA 6 owners who will be playing from the home of hobbits and the haka, for a few hours today at least.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you."

While the New Zealand trick is perfectly safe, it is technically not what the Xbox's region settings were originally designed for. Still, Microsoft has always kept quiet about the manoeuvre — and likely will continue to do so as it seeks every advantage it can take over PlayStation, where the vast majority of GTA 6 copies are expected to be sold.

You can do a version of the New Zealand trick on PS5, but it's more fiddly and there are more hoops to jump through. We've got a breakdown of the New Zealand trick right here if you fancy giving it a shot .

IGN has everything you need for the launch of GTA 6, including the GTA 6 global release times whether you're travelling to New Zealand or not , as well as details on the last-minute PS5 update you'll need to download . In case you missed it, last night we learned the real-life identity of GTA 6's Lucia . And we're now live with our GTA 6 launch blog , which we'll use to fill you in on everything about the game over the coming hours.

articles.title: GTA 6 Photo Mode Confirmed at Launch
articles.summary: GTA 6 has a photo mode included at launch, and it’s fantastic.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is a gorgeous-looking game, so naturally, you’ll feel the urge to pause regularly to take it all in. Thankfully, Rockstar knows this and has included a full-fledged photo mode at launch.

The developer is no stranger to such a concept, with GTA 5 including a whole movie director mode, and Red Dead Redemption 2 eventually gaining a photo mode alongside its PC launch. It’s a pleasant surprise, then, that it's here from the get-go with GTA 6.

It took 70 hours to complete my first playthrough of Jason and Lucia’s story, but I’d be lying if I said a couple of those hours weren’t spent messing around taking pictures when the mood struck me. Sometimes the light bounces perfectly off those waters off Ocean Beach, and you just can’t help but capture the moment.

The photo studio, found by pausing the game and hitting the square button on PS5/X button on Xbox, is impressively well-equipped, too. With aspect ratios, aperture, and depth of field all available to play with when it comes to the camera itself, a variety of different lighting from spotlights to floodlights to softboxes all available to insert into scenes, and a range of post-processing tools including a variety of filters, it’s a relatively impressive suite that I’ve enjoyed playing around with.

That being said, there are a few little things here and there that I’d love to see Rockstar introduce in future updates. Perhaps the primary one of those is the ability to reposition Jason and Lucia into new poses and change their facial expressions. Sometimes you just get that perfect background scenery, but unfortunately one or both of the couple just look bored by the thought of it, and I have to call the photo shoot off. Life’s hard sometimes.

I really am nitpicking, though. Much like the larger game around it, GTA 6’s photo mode is largely impressive, and I’m sure I’ll lose dozens more hours to capturing all of the weird and wonderful sights Vice City and its surrounding areas have to offer.

articles.title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Story Missions — Here’s Why
articles.summary: Unlike previous games in the series, you can't replay missions in GTA 6.
articles.body:
Think you’ll want to replay some of GTA 6 ’s most exciting missions? Well, you won’t be able to simply do that from any of its menus.

Now, not every game allows you to do this, so Rockstar’s latest is by no means an outlier in this regard, but seeing as practically every one of the studio’s games since The Ballad of Gay Tony expansion for GTA 4 has allowed you to do so, it is a little surprising.

GTA 6 is a little different from other games in the series, though. Its story flows and branches in small and big ways in a fluid manner not quite seen in any of the developer’s other open worlds. I’ve only completed one full playthrough myself, but can confirm that whole missions can play out differently based on decisions you didn’t even necessarily know you were making hours earlier. For example, one of GTA 6’s best missions, a daring high-stakes heist, can go relatively smoothly or turn out to be a much messier operation.

What’s most exciting is that, now knowing this, I’m left wondering how many new things I’ll see in the second playthrough I’ve just started, as much as I am looking forward to replaying the missions I can’t easily access. The decision by Rockstar not to include the option to revisit them at launch may well prove controversial, and who knows if it will be added post-launch, but I can see the argument as to why they’ve decided to do it this way.

With so many moving cogs and gears working away in the background to direct Jason and Lucia’s story down certain paths, both within main missions and seemingly random events in the open world, going back to change how certain things played out may prove problematic for its flow. With no medal system implemented — another Rockstar staple that grades your performance on a scale of bronze, silver, and gold — you’d want to replay these missions purely for the fun of it rather than chase high scores or personal best times.

There is one more traditional way around this problem to an extent, though, if you really do feel the urge to revisit moments: save files. GTA 6 gives you room for 15 manual save slots, and I’d highly recommend making a new one every 7% or so through the story so you’re never a million miles from reaching a point you may want to return to. With a main story that can take anywhere from 50 to 100 hours to complete depending on your playstyle, it’s always handy to have the opportunity to return to specific chapters.

articles.title: GTA 6 Switches Sprint to L3, Saving Thumbs Globally
articles.summary: GTA 6 has changed the series' traditional sprint button, moving it to the modern standard of L3.
articles.body:
Ever since Grand Theft Auto made the switch to 3D space with 2001’s GTA 3 , players have had to make use of the X button on PlayStation or the A button on Xbox to sprint. Up until San Andreas , holding down the relevant face button would trigger sprint, but CJ’s story changed that to just meaning “run”, with a repeated tap introduced for a full-fledged sprint. It’s been that way ever since with Rockstar’s games, including most recently 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2 , leaving sore thumbs globally at the end of long chase sequences.

Well now, with GTA 6 , everything has changed.

Finally, Rockstar’s return to Vice City changes the default sprint button to a press of the left analog stick, with a click of L3 making both Jason and Lucia sprint easily. You get the sense that the developer knows what a big deal this is, too, with one of the very first screens you see when first booting up GTA 6 being a warning about this change, alongside a message letting you know you can revert back to a more classic control scheme if you like.

Interestingly, in a fun little easter egg of sorts, there is one instance you’ll have to run where the traditional button mapping does return. In a nod to the series’ past, if you use a treadmill at one of the map’s several gyms, the minigame asks you to repeatedly press down the X/A button at the correct rhythm to score as high as possible. So, if you fancy getting either of the protagonists in great shape, you’ll also be giving your thumb a workout at the same time.

Rockstar’s control schemes have long been a bone of contention for many fans, with RDR2’s in particular feeling unwieldy to some. Many unfortunate NPCs in the Wild West fell victim to accidental trigger pulls when all Arthur wanted to do was greet them with a pull of the left trigger and a button press. Although GTA 6 uses a similar communication system with the population of its world, thankfully pulling out a gun in public is a much more deliberate act in Leonida, and I’m happy to report I’ve not shot the face off of someone yet when all I wanted to do was say hello in over 100 hours so far.

Although I grew up playing in Rockstar’s open worlds, and am thoroughly used to the old-school way of having to sprint, I’d be lying if I didn’t massively prefer this new L3 approach to toggling a faster run speed. For a studio that always feels at the forefront of moving game development forward whenever it releases a game, the repeated tapping of X always felt like a needless and stubbornly archaic button input to me. Thankfully, my thumbs were instead saved for all of the delights Vice City had in store for me.

articles.title: How Long Is GTA 6?
articles.summary: We knew GTA 6's campaign would be big, but how long does it take to complete? We tasked four people with playing it start to finish to find out.
articles.body:
In every sense of the word, Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive game. But just how much time will you have to set aside to see all of it? Well, that could potentially take years given the size of its map and the incredible amount of detail packed into it – we’re still exploring to find its many hidden secrets, hours after finishing the main mission chain. What we can give you an idea of, though, is just how long it took us to finish the story.

We’ve gathered playtimes from four different writers from across IGN and our sister websites, Eurogamer and Pure Xbox , in order to showcase just how much that hour total can vary. Here’s how long it took us to beat GTA 6, the playstyles each player opted for, and what they prioritised their time doing.

Our fastest player finished GTA 6 in 42 hours.

Our “slowest” player took 115 hours to see the credits roll.

Everyone plays games differently, so read on for more details about how everyone played, how long it took to reach the credits, and some of their unique thoughts about the game's length. Once you've finished the game yourself, be sure to submit your times on How Long To Beat and see how your time compares!

GTA 6 is a big game. So big, in fact, that even the 70 hours it took me to reach the end credits felt rushed at times. I started off sticking to the critical path, mainly focusing on Jason and Lucia’s main missions in Chapter 1, as I didn’t quite know how long the journey ahead was going to take me. To some extent, this whole opening act feels like an extended tutorial, and once the game really finds its rhythm in Chapter 2, I began to take things a little steadier, making sure to complete all optional missions before moving on to the next slice of story. This method of playing continued until I reached the end. Well, the first of many endings I have found so far. I’m not sure how many ways the couple’s tale can wrap up, but I’ve found four so far. I’ll leave what those are, and how you get them, up to you to find out, though.

Upon first finishing at that 70-hour mark, I had achieved 71% of GTA 6’s 100% checklist, meaning there were still plenty of activities to do, collectibles to find, cars to steal, and people to meet left for me in Leonida. I’ve since put in another 30 hours and only pushed 1% further, as I’ve been slowly exploring the vast map that stretches well beyond Vice City. There are a ludicrous number of collectibles to find in this game, including hundreds of playing cards, which really do feel like finding a needle in a haystack each and every time you stumble across them.

Those shall wait for another day, though. As will achieving that full 100%. For now, I’ve started a fresh save, already making my way through Chapter 1 again in an effort to see how GTA 6’s story changes and the missions within it branch when you try to keep Jason and Lucia’s relationship as frosty as possible. I won’t lie, though, it’s tough. Rockstar has done a phenomenal job at building a bond between them, and in my original 70 hours I was compelled to keep them at a full “hot together” relationship rating, so having to tear them out of my heart now feels quite painful. It’s all in the name of science, I guess.

With the extraordinarily rare luxury of having more than three weeks to play through Grand Theft Auto 6 in order to write IGN’s review , I was actually able to move through it in pretty much precisely the same sort of way I would’ve if I’d been playing exclusively for pleasure. For me, this means allowing myself to be constantly distracted by minigames, exploring interesting areas, and stopping for every stranger I encounter. There was really no point where I ever ignored doing something I felt like doing because I felt obligated to tackle a story mission instead. As a result, it took me 115 hours to reach GTA 6’s finale.

My Jason and Lucia maintained a professional criminal rating throughout thanks to my style of play, where I typically opt for non-lethal takedowns against general law enforcement, disabling vehicles by popping tyres rather than pummeling the windscreens with gunfire, and leaving civilians alone. By the end of the story, I had actually only killed 11 civilians, all of whom were accidents.

I’ve seen two endings so far, and my overall completion rate is at 72% now that I’ve reached the end of the story, but I feel I’m likely to simply start again at this point rather than push this save to 100%. This is because I actually really want to experience it from the beginning again, only slower . More racing, more fishing, more exploring; I want to see how long it’ll take me without a deadline – even if that deadline was a surprisingly generous one. And can I reach the end without killing a single civilian? I’m about to find out.

Chris Tapsell — Editor in Chief, Eurogamer

It took me about 65 hours to complete GTA 6's story, which I expect to be on the faster end compared to most other reviewers, and there's a bit of a caveat which explains that, too: I opted to really focus hard on the main story and character-based side missions in the final quarter of it or so. For a short while, towards the end, I actually got in-game taxis between missions to "fast travel" and speed progress up, partially to test how that might affect the game world – so much of the game is discovered while travelling; what happens if you skip that? – and partially just so I could make sure I got to the end in time.

Saying that, I've still done all of the character-based side missions that I'm aware of, and just have a few of the more significant questlines that come from 'emergent events' to get through (although I get the sense there are dozens and dozens of smaller one-off versions of these still to see). There are still corners of the map to properly explore, and I've only scraped the surface of some systems like fishing, diving, and racing. Between hitting your savings goals and doing all of the side activities, let alone just hanging out and following your interests as you go, I'd still need well over a hundred hours with it. I wouldn't expect many people to finish the story in under 70 hours and honestly wouldn't recommend it either. Take your time with it – the game's at its best when it's played slow!

The vast majority of my time in Leonida has been spent with the main campaign missions, akin to what you might call a mainline, even “rushed” playthrough. It took me exactly 42 hours to finish Jason and Lucia's story, and a handful of those hours were spent doing optional activities like side missions, playing minigolf, stealing motorised scooters, and simply wandering around the huge metropolis that is Vice City.

That might sound disappointing if you were expecting a 100+ ﻿hour epic, or if you were putting a lot of stock into the quote that mentioned 80 hours a few months ago, but this isn't the kind of game you ideally want to rush. Take your time with it, explore the ridiculously impressive open-world, and allow it to divert your attention towards any number of activities that aren't directly connected to the main storyline. ﻿There's so much more to do beyond just the core campaign, and I reckon some players will easily reach 80 hours or more before they get to the end credits.

Now that I've hustled my way through it for the Pure Xbox review , my plan is to go back through the campaign at a much slower pace over the next few weeks and months, and I can't wait to see what surprises I missed the first time around. There are parts of the map I haven't even visited yet!

So, that’s how long it took each of us to finish GTA 6’s main story. How are you planning to play Rockstar’s latest? And how are you going to play as Jason and Lucia? In or out of love? As violent psychos or clean professionals? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: GTA 6: How The Ultimate Edition Content Works
articles.summary: Some of GTA 6’s Ultimate Edition content can only be used in certain story chapters - here's how it works.
articles.body:
Ever since pre-orders for GTA 6 went live and its $100 Ultimate Edition was revealed, one question has been asked more than any other: Is it worth it?

Well, if our poll ran at the time is any indication, 70% of you certainly felt that way, with the majority opting for the full GTA 6 experience over the standard version.

We’ve long known what is included in the more expensive edition, from personalised vehicles and weapons to exclusive stores and missions. But what we didn’t know was how exactly we’d access this extra stuff or when we’d be able to use it. Well, now we do, thanks to the details listed in the in-game store, which states, “Ultimate Edition bonuses are threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia’s Story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter”.

It turns out that these extras will be sprinkled throughout the story, unlocking over the course of its chapters, with some only being available to use during certain timeframes, and even permanently removing your access to them once you pass points in Jason and Lucia’s tale.

Here’s the full list of the bonuses and when you’ll be able to get your hands on each:

Jason’s Vehicles – An army fatigue-tinged Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak. Only available from Jason’s house for use during Chapter 1 .

Ganado Retro Build – Jason’s Vapid Ganado low-riding pickup with exclusive mods. Apply at the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. Only available to use in Chapter 1.

Personalised Weapon Variants – Sidearms with detailed engravings for Jason’s Girardi ES9 and Lucia’s Klose K17 pistols. Found in the variants section of the weapon locker at Ammu-Nation. Jason’s is available from Chapter 1. Lucia’s is available in Chapter 2.

Morgan Revolvers – His and hers versions of the revolver with classic Vice City stylings, sourced from the Vercetti Estate. Available from any Ammu-Nation weapon locker in Chapter 2.

One-Eyed Willie’s – A mod shop in Lake Leonida specialising in off-road modifications and hand-painted art. Available from Chapter 1.

Dominator Buggy & Garage – An off-road buggy built for the terrain of Mount Kalaga and its surrounding areas, which can be stored in the Paradise Garage in Watson Bay. Available after visiting the Mud Club with Wyman in Chapter 2.

Classic Car Collection – A string of side objectives that task you with tracking down abandoned classic cars for Wyman to restore them to their former glory. Wyman will contact you on WhatUp once you’ve collected the Dominator in Chapter 2.

Rideout Customs – A mod shop exclusive to the Ultimate Edition that specialises in detailed interiors, rims, and donk stylings. Available from Chapter 1.

PTT Youngin$ Compound – A gang compound you can raid in the Southside area of Vice City, full of special items and distinct contraband. Available from Chapter 1 once you’ve explored Southside.

Stock 305 Clothing Store – A clothing store in the Stockyard area of Vice City with elevated streetwear styles available for Jason and Lucia. Available from Chapter 1.

Sara’s Unisex Salon – A hair salon in Hamlet with signature styles for both Jason and Lucia, including facial hair for Jason and makeup and nails for Lucia. Available from Chapter 1. Signature looks available from Chapter 2.

Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor – Located in Stockyard with over 50 signature tattoo styles for both Jason and Lucia, all designed by the artist collective FAILE. Available from Chapter 1.

Vice City Merch – A collection of apparel inspired by the in-game TV show character, Macca the Gator. Available from the mannequins at The Wonder Whale in Key Lento.

Vice City Style – Exclusive outfits, tattoos, and more for Jason and Lucia. Available in your wardrobe, most tattoo parlors, and at Sara’s Unisex Salon from Chapter 4 .

Shitzu Squalo – A gradient pink and blue boat equipped with an explosives-laden weapons crate. Available from the Washington Beach canal dock in Chapter 4.

‘95 Grotti Cheetah – A signature sports car with a white and red retro-futuristic livery. Available from the Pegassi Residences building in Chapter 5.

So, enjoy those early Jason vehicles while you can, as once they’re gone, they’re gone forever. Most of the bonuses are available from early on, though, and remain there for you to use throughout the whole of your adventure through Leonida. Just one word of advice: even though you can visit some places, such as Stock 305 clothing, you may not have the cash early on to actually afford anything there. It’s a pricey place.

Are you happy with how the exclusive Ultimate Edition content is spread throughout GTA 6? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: 'GTA Flu' Trends Online as Reports Suggest Thousands Will Skip School and Call in Sick at Work, With a Measurable Hit to Country's Economies
articles.summary: As GTA 6 launches around the world, businesses are bracing for a wave of so-called "GTA flu" as staff call in sick to play Rockstar's hugely-anticipated video game.
articles.body:
As GTA 6 launches around the world, businesses are bracing for a wave of so-called "GTA flu" as staff call in sick to play Rockstar's hugely-anticipated video game.

The U.K.'s National Health Service has even issued guidance on how to stay healthy over the coming days and weeks, as millions begin long gaming sessions to explore Vice City. "Planning on dedicating time to gaming later this week?" reads a post by the NHS on Instagram .

"Try and take regular breaks, obviously. And be mindful of RSI (repetitive strain injury). That’s a term for pain that can be caused by repeated movement of part of the body, such as hands and fingers. Search online for 'NHS RSI' to get some advice on how to avoid getting any injuries."

Whether you're risking calling in sick to work or taking an unplanned day off from school, concern over the impact of GTA flu is spreading, particularly among teachers and parents. A school in Norwich, England has issued a warning about pupils declaring they have "GTA flu", Norfolk's Evening News reports, following a spate of similar messages to parents set out by schools across the U.K. and Ireland earlier this week. One school is even offering gift cards as an incentive for students to actually show up .

In Australia, requests for annual leave have reportedly jumped 29% around launch day compared to the same time period last year, News24 noted, with men aged 18 to 44 making up 75% of those vacation requests. According to The Sydney Morning Herald , meanwhile, GTA 6's launch is expected to cost the Australian enconomy at least $70 million, as it's expected that at least 1 in every 100 workers will call in sick.

U.K. tabloid The Daily Star claimed that "massive workplace carnage" would take place on both sides of the Atlantic, with 1.5 million US staff and 2.1 million U.K. employees expected to be absent, albeit via booking the day off. This could, the paper reported, drain U.S. national output "by 2% per cent in a single day, costing the American economy a staggering $1 billion in lost productivity."

While the flurry of excitement around GTA 6 may seem extreme to some, others would argue that this is a moment in gaming like no other — the launch of a fresh entry in an industry-defining franchise for the first time in over a decade, and after multiple high-profile delays. Indeed, even Strauss Zelnick, head of GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive, previously said he expected "a whole lot of people calling in sick on November 19."

articles.title: GTA 6: 15 Minutes of First Mission Gameplay
articles.summary: Check out 15 minutes of gameplay from the first mission of GTA 6 captured on PS5 Pro.
articles.body:
It’s finally here. GTA 6 is now available to play for both physical and virtual residents of New Zealand, and we’ve got a brand new slice of gameplay for you to check out. While the video below may not be the very first minutes of Rockstar’s latest Grand Theft Auto, it is taken from the first proper mission of the game, which takes place after a short prologue. The reason for this? We think it would be nice for you to experience the start of the story for yourself, and it means we can avoid any potentially cool reveals or spoilers in that story-heavy prologue and focus on the gameplay itself.

In the roughly 15-minute section, you’ll see Jason, alongside his friends Cal and Donnie, complete a little drug-running operation near Key Lento — part of GTA 6’s fictional Florida Keys archipelago. You’ll get to check out just how stupidly gorgeous that water looks, a blend of both stealth takedowns and loud gunplay action, as well as some of that trademark Rockstar humour. Enjoy!

articles.title: GTA 6 Uses FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S to Upscale From 720p to 1080p
articles.summary: GTA 6 is finally here, and it's genuinely a technical marvel on all of the consoles it's running on. It's particularly impressive that the Xbox Series S can even run the thing, and now we know a bit more about how Rockstar was able to pull it off.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is finally here, and it's genuinely a technical marvel on all of the consoles it's running on. It's particularly impressive that the Xbox Series S can even run the thing, and now we know a bit more about how Rockstar was able to pull it off.

Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, according to an interview with Wccftech . That would make GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox, and it's probably what made the game possible on the budget console.

I've already spent a bit of time with the Xbox Series S version of GTA 6, and while it does look a bit rough around the edges (literally), it looks better than I was expecting. Objects in the game are still incredibly detailed, but the edges of some objects – particularly distant buildings and hair – have a noticeable sheen of aliasing around them. But that lower resolution rendering is what lets the game mostly sit at around 30fps (though I did notice a couple drops down to the mid-20s.)

According to the interview, the Xbox Series S is the only version of the game that's running on FSR 4. Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game are instead using Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro is using PSSR 2.0. It shouldn't be surprising either, that the Xbox Series S is also running at the lowest input resolution out of all of the consoles at 720p, compared to 1440p on all of the other consoles.

When Wccftech asked Rockstar about the reasons it picked each upscaling solution, it said: "Part of that process [of targeting 30fps] was determining our base resolution and upscaling solution. We evaluated a variety of approaches for each console, then selected a combination of each that gave us the look and performance we needed." And, well, despite some noisy surfaces and aliasing, FSR 4 absolutely let Rockstar hit that 30fps target on the Xbox Series S.

Either way, GTA 6 is clearly a massive success. It's already the best-reviewed game of all time on Metacritic, and here at IGN we gave it a 10, with reviewer Luke Reilly saying: "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

We're also live blogging GTA 6's launch , in what is surely going to be the biggest release in gaming history.

articles.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' could be the biggest entertainment launch in history, preorders top $1.65 billion
articles.summary: Take-Two Interactive's 'GTA VI' is shaping up to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history.
articles.body:
If your office is surprisingly empty or fewer people are messaging you than normal on Thursday, there's a decent chance it's because your colleagues are some of the millions diving into Take-Two Interactive's ( TTWO ) "Grand Theft Auto VI."

According to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, "GTA VI" has already generated more than $1.65 billion in preorder sales, an unprecedented amount for a game.

Some 75% of those sales have been on Sony's ( SONY ) PlayStation 5, while the remainder were on Microsoft's ( MSFT ) Xbox Series S and X consoles.

"The only real limitation on what this game can do at the moment is the install base of PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles," Circana executive director of games Mat Piscatella told Yahoo Finance.

"There are billboards. There are TV commercials in the World Series. They've got local news covering the game. The Weather Channel is posting clips," he added. "This is well beyond the reach of a normal even hit video game."

It's been 13 years since publisher Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games released "Grand Theft Auto V" in September 2013 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360.

Despite that, Piscatella explained, the game has remained among the top 20 bestselling titles every single month.

Take-Two says it has sold roughly 235 million copies of "GTA V" as of its November earnings report, and that it "reached $1 billion in retail sales faster than any entertainment release in history."

While "GTA VI" is widely expected to be a hit beyond its pre-order numbers, gamers looking to purchase a new PlayStation or Xbox to play the title may be in for some sticker shock.

Console prices have surged due to tariffs and the memory and storage crisis, making them far less affordable than prior generations.

A PlayStation 5 without a disc drive launched at $399 in November 2020. Today, it costs $599 . A version with a disc drive that launched at $499 now costs $649 .

Microsoft's Xbox Series S originally cost $299, and is now $499, while the Series X climbed $250 to $749 .

"Back in September of 2013, when 'Grand Theft Auto V' launched, a PlayStation 3 was going for $250, and an [Xbox] 360 was going for $230, which, inflation-adjusted, is roughly $350," Piscatella said.

"So even inflation-adjusted, these consoles are now $300 more expensive than they were in 2013 when 'Grand Theft Auto V' launched."

articles.title: MindsEye Dev Build a Rocket Boy Says Legal Action Against 'Several Third Parties' Will Help It Pay Off Its Mountain of Debt
articles.summary: After the disastrous release of MindsEye, its collapsed developer, Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), is attempting to pay off its mountain of debt via legal action against “saboteurs” who it alleged contributed to the game's downfall.
articles.body:
After the disastrous release of MindsEye , its collapsed developer, Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), is attempting to pay off its mountain of debt via legal action against “saboteurs” who it alleged contributed to the game's downfall.

Story-driven action adventure game MindsEye was initially designed to be a part of Everywhere, the ‘Roblox for adults’ creation platform led by former Grand Theft Auto design chief Leslie Benzies. BARB eventually switched to focus on MindsEye, with the company ballooning in size to over 500 staff at peak.

But MindsEye flopped hard when it came out in June 2025, with players calling it "broken," "buggy," and "the worst game of 2025." Soon after, BARB said it was “heartbroken” over the issues players had faced with the game , and promised to release a series of patches to fix the significant performance problems, glitches, and AI behavior bugs. Amid sweeping layoffs, Benzies told staff that the studio would bounce back and relaunch MindsEye, blaming its struggles on internal and external "saboteurs," among other things. CEO Mark Gerhard said the studio had been investigating what he called “criminal activity” that took place around the launch of the game.

However, in September this year it was reported that the Edinburgh-based company faced closure, with BARB slipping into administration. Today, on the eve of GTA 6's launch, an administrators’ proposal went live on BARB’s Companies House page — spotted by RedbullCola on ResetEra , (thanks Kotaku ). The proposal details what BARB owes and to who, as well as how it plans to cover its debts.

The total debt comes to £61.7 million (approx. $81.2 million). The bulk of the debt belongs to NetEase (£36.4 million, approx. $47.9 million). NetEase is a major investor in BARB, having participated in multiple funding rounds including a $110 million Series D round in January 2024. According to company documents , BARB brought in more than £233 million (approx. $306 million) of investment by 2024. £19.90 (approx. $25... yes, $25!) is owed to ChatGPT company OpenAI.

Earlier this year, BARB co-CEO Mark Gerhard claimed the studio was a victim of corporate espionage and "saboteurs." The company will now pursue litigation against the people it accused in a bid to gather the money and pay off the debts. Gerhard had pinned the blame on a YouTube and TikTok management agency called Ritual Network, accusing it of tarnishing BARB’s reputation in a coordinated propaganda campaign. Ritual Network has denied all allegations that it orchestrated a $1 million smear campaign against MindsEye.

The proposal claims BARB’s investigations against “a number of third parties” are “the largest asset of the administration,” so it seems like all hopes at the company of paying off the debt are tied to litigation being successful.

Here is BARB's claim from the company document filed today:

In May, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, issued what sounded like a nod to BARB’s struggles . "Making hits seems to get harder and harder and harder as entertainment industries mature," Zelnick said, speaking at the TD Cowen 54th Annual Technology, Media & Telecom Conference.

"The folks at Rockstar seem to be able to make these massive hits, and lots of other people have tried. Lots and lots, including former Rockstar employees. And so far, they haven't been able to do it."
